statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of four public templates plus the 404 recovery path.

page.framework: server-rendered MPA with third-party advertising/consent scripts
page.notes: Public Vietnamese lottery results, statistics and editorial site. Not covered: authenticated account internals, every province/day variant, purchase/subscription flows (none on selected public journey), and exhaustive offline simulation; shared templates were de-duplicated.

Results template at 390x844 with consent wall.
Statistics form at 390x844 with consent wall.
Homepage under dark and reduced-motion preferences; UI remains light.
Article and consent UI remain legible in forced colors.
Article layout metrics report 106px horizontal overflow and two long tasks.
Homepage trace summary: LCP 3.68s in trace.
Homepage HAR with 55 requests and 2.44MB transferred.
HAR summary: 51 third-party requests and 2.41MB third-party bytes.
Client-side secret scan; only expected public Firebase key found.
Image dimensions, loading and format audit.
Heap summary after ten menu-toggle attempts.
Dark/reduced-motion and modern CSS feature probe.
Rendered homepage DOM and computed-style capture.
Homepage route, heading, metadata, form and dialog recon.
Article semantics, targets, focus and CSS probe.
Statistics form labels and control probe.
Service-worker registration probe returned an empty list.
Purposeful 404 response with home recovery link.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark/reduced screenshot remains a white/cream light theme; the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and no authored prefers-color-scheme rule.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated reduced motion and inspected active animations
checkOutcomes.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reported zero active animations; no auto-advance or essential animated flow was present.
Text, links, controls and consent actions remain visibly differentiated under forced-colors active.
The CSS probe found no authored view-transition rule or startViewTransition use across this multi-page site.
No parallax, scrollytelling, reveal animation or other scroll-linked motion exists to implement declaratively.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, reveal animation or other scroll-linked motion exists to implement declaratively.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Core pages rely on native page scrolling and links; no custom swipe/pointer interaction was found fighting platform behavior.
The 8,518px homepage and 5,816px article use fixed shared chrome, but the CSS probe found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline behavior.
No tooltip/popover/menu requiring element-relative anchor positioning was present on the audited core paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip/popover/menu requiring element-relative anchor positioning was present on the audited core paths.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed navigation, breadcrumbs and first viewports
checkOutcomes.evidence: Article breadcrumbs, descriptive links, red active navigation and direct result links give users visible orientation.
Desktop, homepage mobile, results, and statistics screenshots all show a modal consent wall covering the lottery results or form before interaction.
DOM recon found multiple `div[role=dialog]` consent surfaces rather than native `<dialog>`, while the modal injects hundreds of vendor headings into the document.
The consent interface lists 210 partners and the tracker probe sees 17 third-party origins; article Lighthouse also loads in-article advertising controls around the content.
At a 390px visual viewport, article layout metrics report scrollWidth/client layout width 496px and horizontalOverflowPx 106.
The article CSS probe found no authored `@container` rule despite cards, sidebars and result tables being reused across narrow and wide regions.
The focused first link computed to `outline-style:none`; the probe also found multiple visible targets under 24px high.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed first viewports and heading/link hierarchy
checkOutcomes.evidence: The H1 and result tables immediately identify current three-region lottery results, with direct regional result links.

checkOutcomes.method: Walked home to results and statistics surfaces
checkOutcomes.evidence: Current results are readable without sign-in and regional/history links use real destinations; the primary lookup does not dead-end.

checkOutcomes.method: Requested an unknown route and inspected recovery state
checkOutcomes.evidence: The server returns HTTP 404 with a clear bilingual not-found message, home link and alternative region links.
Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 11.1s, TTI 11.5s and performance 67; the independent trace measured LCP 3.68s.
CLS was 0.013 home, 0.060 results, 0.028 stats and 0.063 article, all within the good threshold.
Article Lighthouse measured 530ms TBT and 28.6s TTI; mobile layout observed 90ms and 52ms long tasks.
HAR recorded 2.44MB, including 2.21MB of scripts; 2.41MB came from third parties and a 414KB Prebid script was uncompressed.
Lighthouse estimated 624KiB unused JS on home and 2,034KiB on the article, including duplicated gtag/ad stacks.
Article Lighthouse found six ad links with no discernible name; the statistics probe found date/select/button controls with no associated labels.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility plus forced-colors visual review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 100 on home and 97 on article without a reported contrast failure; forced colors remains readable.
The page probe found no visible outline on the first focused link and consent markup injects several H1s plus hundreds of vendor H2s into the document.
Article body uses large black text on white, clear hierarchy and comfortable line spacing in the visible reading column.
The article has 106px horizontal overflow at 390px, and the interaction probe found multiple targets under 24px high.
Lighthouse reported “Not signed in with the identity provider” as a console error on home and article.
The image primitive found 21 of 25 images without width/height; 10 below-fold images were not lazy-loaded.
Lighthouse failed notification-on-start on both representative pages; article ads also triggered a deprecated Shared Storage warning.
Home and article have descriptive unique titles and meta descriptions; Lighthouse passes both title and description audits.
Lighthouse found `a#curr_living_btn` labelled “➜ Xem ngay” with `href="javascript:void(0)"`.
Both pages return 200, homepage has canonical URL, robots is valid and sitemap.xml is available without accidental noindex.
Homepage exposes Organization and WebSite JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter title, description and image matching visible content.
HTTPS is used, but headers lack CSP, HSTS and nosniff; all seven observed first-party cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
Tracker evidence found 17 third-party origins and six known trackers; HAR attributes 51/55 requests and 2.41/2.44MB to third parties before a consent choice.
Lighthouse identified a notification permission request on page load. The sign-in surface exists, but no passkey flow was exposed in the audited public path.
Header audit found no HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; only X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN was present.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared raw HTML, crawler screenshot and rendered DOM
checkOutcomes.evidence: Core results and article text are server-rendered without JS; home raw/rendered token coverage is 72% and neither page is a JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Exercised representative pages and edge states
checkOutcomes.evidence: Results, statistics, article and 404 pages render useful content; no clipped core overlay/menu or blank runtime state was observed.
This public results/content site is not a long-lived app requiring offline use; a manifest exists but no service-worker registration was found.
checkOutcomes.reason: This public results/content site is not a long-lived app requiring offline use; a manifest exists but no service-worker registration was found.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The server returns a real 404 and a useful recovery page with a homepage link and suggested result destinations.
The document declares `lang="vi"`; Vietnamese text renders in the expected LTR reading order.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed site scope and rendered data
checkOutcomes.evidence: The service deliberately targets Vietnamese lottery data in one locale and exposes no currency or user-selectable locale requiring cross-locale formatting.
checkOutcomes.reason: The service deliberately targets Vietnamese lottery data in one locale and exposes no currency or user-selectable locale requiring cross-locale formatting.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Published draw/article dates are local Vietnamese dates; no cross-time-zone scheduling or user-entered time flow is present.
checkOutcomes.reason: Published draw/article dates are local Vietnamese dates; no cross-time-zone scheduling or user-entered time flow is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed consent UI and core flow
checkOutcomes.evidence: Consent and Do not consent are equally prominent and the public result flow does not force account creation, purchase or continuity.
The audited public statistics flow has no required free-form submission or validation error state; login was outside the selected public core flow.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited public statistics flow has no required free-form submission or validation error state; login was outside the selected public core flow.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The statistics form probe found an unlabeled text date, unlabeled select and button, all with empty autocomplete values.
No checkout, subscription, payment, account-management or sensitive account action is part of the audited public lottery lookup journey.
checkOutcomes.reason: No checkout, subscription, payment, account-management or sensitive account action is part of the audited public lottery lookup journey.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Image evidence reports 21 missing dimensions, 10 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and two images without responsive sources.
HAR shows 51 third-party requests and 2.21MB of scripts for a mostly text/table page; Lighthouse estimates up to 2MB unused JS on the article.
2.41MB of 2.44MB transferred on home was third party; top costs were tag manager, Prebid, ads, MGID and consent code.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected public purpose and agent APIs
checkOutcomes.evidence: The site exposes public informational content rather than an agent-facing transaction/tool surface; WebMCP is not necessary for its declared experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site exposes public informational content rather than an agent-facing transaction/tool surface; WebMCP is not necessary for its declared experience.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected functionality and built-in AI surfaces
checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarization, generation or translation task is offered where on-device inference would be an expected product capability.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarization, generation or translation task is offered where on-device inference would be an expected product capability.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared baseline and post-interaction heap summaries after ten menu-toggle attempts
checkOutcomes.evidence: Self size changed from 31.93MB to 32.72MB across separate fresh sessions; this does not establish unbounded retained growth, but confidence is low because third-party load variance dominates.
Baseline heap summary contains 575,957 nodes and 31.9MB self size, while the DOM probe counts 6,798 elements; third-party ad/consent code dominates the complexity.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared heap constructor summaries and sampled inline listeners
checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither heap top-constructor list contains Detached* nodes; the runtime probe found one inline listener-bearing element and no evidence of accumulating detached DOM.

principleOutcomes.reason: The site has no applicable agent-facing capability for this contextual principle.

paths.description: Homepage and current-results overview; represents the primary task and shared site chrome.
Northern lottery result listing; represents the core results template.
Loto statistics tool; represents the primary form/interactive analysis journey.
Analysis article; represents editorial content, ad embedding, crawlability and long-form mobile layout.
Unknown URL; exercises HTTP failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: Consent wall obscures the primary content on first load
findings.evidence: Desktop, homepage mobile, results, and statistics screenshots all show a modal consent wall covering the lottery results or form before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where legally possible; keep equal accept/reject controls and preserve access to core content.

findings.summary: Article template overflows mobile by 106px
findings.evidence: At a 390px visual viewport, article layout metrics report scrollWidth/client layout width 496px and horizontalOverflowPx 106.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the minimum/fixed width causing 496px layout; use `max-inline-size:100%`, fluid tables/media and wrapping.

findings.summary: Homepage LCP is far outside the good range
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 11.1s, TTI 11.5s and performance 67; the independent trace measured LCP 3.68s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, delay consent/ad scripts until needed, and retest under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Article scripting blocks interaction
findings.evidence: Article Lighthouse measured 530ms TBT and 28.6s TTI; mobile layout observed 90ms and 52ms long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up first-party work and defer or remove advertising/video scripts until the associated slot approaches the viewport.

findings.summary: Third-party script delivery dominates the load
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 2.44MB, including 2.21MB of scripts; 2.41MB came from third parties and a 414KB Prebid script was uncompressed.
findings.suggestedFix: Load only essential critical resources, compress all text, gate ad stacks behind consent/visibility and remove duplicate analytics tags.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript are unused
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 624KiB unused JS on home and 2,034KiB on the article, including duplicated gtag/ad stacks.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tags and route/slot-condition ad dependencies so code is fetched only where it adds value.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow and target sizing fail on the article
findings.evidence: The article has 106px horizontal overflow at 390px, and the interaction probe found multiple targets under 24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix narrow reflow, preserve user zoom, and enlarge target hit areas without relying on text glyph dimensions.

findings.summary: The page requests notifications on load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed notification-on-start on both representative pages; article ads also triggered a deprecated Shared Storage warning.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask for notifications only after an explicit user action and update or remove third-party code using deprecated APIs.

findings.summary: Core transport defenses and cookie flags are missing
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but headers lack CSP, HSTS and nosniff; all seven observed first-party cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and secure appropriate SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.summary: The initial page has an excessive tracking footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 17 third-party origins and six known trackers; HAR attributes 51/55 requests and 2.41/2.44MB to third parties before a consent choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics/ad requests until consent, consolidate vendors, minimize identifiers and batch essential measurement.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested out of context
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified a notification permission request on page load. The sign-in surface exists, but no passkey flow was exposed in the audited public path.
findings.suggestedFix: Move notification requests behind a clearly explained user action; for account flows, offer WebAuthn/passkeys where practical.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are incomplete
findings.evidence: Header audit found no HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; only X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and a nonce/hash CSP including frame-ancestors, plus nosniff, strict referrer and least-privilege permissions policies.

findings.summary: Background advertising work is disproportionate to the core page
findings.evidence: HAR shows 51 third-party requests and 2.21MB of scripts for a mostly text/table page; Lighthouse estimates up to 2MB unused JS on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize ad auctions, analytics and video players until consent and viewport/user intent require them.

findings.summary: Third-party bytes overwhelm first-party content
findings.evidence: 2.41MB of 2.44MB transferred on home was third party; top costs were tag manager, Prebid, ads, MGID and consent code.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove redundant vendors, and defer media/ad stacks below the fold.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced screenshot remains a white/cream light theme; the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and no authored prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `color-scheme: light dark` and theme surfaces with `light-dark()` or a prefers-color-scheme media query.

findings.summary: Consent UI is custom dialog chrome
findings.evidence: DOM recon found multiple `div[role=dialog]` consent surfaces rather than native `<dialog>`, while the modal injects hundreds of vendor headings into the document.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real modal `<dialog>` with `showModal()`, inert background behavior, focus restoration and a clear close/reject action.

findings.summary: Advertising and consent chrome compete with content
findings.evidence: The consent interface lists 210 partners and the tracker probe sees 17 third-party origins; article Lighthouse also loads in-article advertising controls around the content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce ad slots and vendor chrome, especially above and inside the primary result/article content.

findings.summary: Shared components only use viewport-level adaptation
findings.evidence: The article CSS probe found no authored `@container` rule despite cards, sidebars and result tables being reused across narrow and wide regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare container contexts for reusable result cards/forms and adapt columns, typography and controls with size container queries.

findings.summary: Focus and target sizing are inconsistent
findings.evidence: The focused first link computed to `outline-style:none`; the probe also found multiple visible targets under 24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong `:focus-visible` ring and ensure interactive targets are at least 24px, preferably 44px for primary touch actions.

findings.summary: Some article and statistics controls lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Article Lighthouse found six ad links with no discernible name; the statistics probe found date/select/button controls with no associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic label and require ad creatives to expose meaningful link names or remove them from the tab order.

findings.summary: Injected consent structure and focus styling weaken navigation
findings.evidence: The page probe found no visible outline on the first focused link and consent markup injects several H1s plus hundreds of vendor H2s into the document.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep consent headings inside a correctly labelled dialog without polluting page hierarchy, and add visible `:focus-visible` styles.

findings.summary: Most images lack intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 21 of 25 images without width/height; 10 below-fold images were not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and use native lazy loading for below-fold content images.

findings.summary: A visible action uses a non-crawlable JavaScript URL
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found `a#curr_living_btn` labelled “➜ Xem ngay” with `href="javascript:void(0)"`.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real destination URL for navigation, or a `<button>` when the action is in-page behavior.

findings.summary: Statistics inputs provide little programmatic assistance
findings.evidence: The statistics form probe found an unlabeled text date, unlabeled select and button, all with empty autocomplete values.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native date semantics consistently, visible labels, stable names and relevant autocomplete tokens where user data is entered.

findings.summary: Heap footprint is high for a mostly text/table page
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contains 575,957 nodes and 31.9MB self size, while the DOM probe counts 6,798 elements; third-party ad/consent code dominates the complexity.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce third-party runtimes and consent/ad DOM, unload offscreen ad widgets, and monitor heap/DOM budgets in long sessions.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no authored view-transition rule or startViewTransition use across this multi-page site.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` for eligible same-origin pages, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide static rather than scroll-aware navigation
findings.evidence: The 8,518px homepage and 5,816px article use fixed shared chrome, but the CSS probe found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky header with a compact scrolled state and a lightweight progress/return affordance for long pages.

findings.summary: Identity integration logs a browser error
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported “Not signed in with the identity provider” as a console error on home and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle the signed-out identity state without logging an error; initialize sign-in only where its UI is used.

findings.summary: Image loading metadata is incomplete
findings.evidence: Image evidence reports 21 missing dimensions, 10 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and two images without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, lazy loading and responsive/modern sources for content images while retaining SVG UI assets.
